decisions.reason: It builds directly on established plug-in and data format expertise, its dedicated web page signals early traction, and the firm's own R&D provides high absorptive capacity to improve it.
Digital twin services extend the firm's established geospatial offerings, and its related knowledge plus active R&D cooperation lets it assimilate early market feedback and refine the service.

Although authentication and identity delegation is close to existing GIS integration work, it partially overlaps with the newer identity service, so absorptive capacity supports keeping it but with some rationalization risk.
An open GIS application development framework leverages the firm's core software component knowledge, and its R&D experience enables it to interpret developer feedback and iterate.

The identity and access service integrates directly with GeoIT applications as highlighted at launch, closely matches existing integration capabilities, and benefits from strong in-house R&D to improve it.
